newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia wants grain output at 95 mln tonnes by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Russia wants grain output at 95 mln tonnes by 2000.

text.p: Russia hopes to return grain output to levels seen earlier this decade, mainly through greater private sector output and better use of soil, Interfax mews agency quoted industry specialists as saying on Friday.
Specialists at the Agriculture Ministry and All-Russian Institute of Agricultural Economy said net grain output could rise to 95 million tonnes a year by 2000.
They said private farms would produce eight to 12 percent of output in coming years, up from five percent at present.

Russia's agriculture sector is in crisis, with 1993 net output of 99.1 million tonnes followed by 81.3 million in 1994 and 63.4 million in 1995. This year's output is forecast at around 70 million tonnes.
Analysts proposed better use of Russia's extremely varied climate and soil and said 94 percent of the winter wheat crop should be sown in the Northern Caucasus and Central Black Earth regions.
Spring wheat, which Interfax said accounted for up to 96 percent of the wheat crop, should be planted in the Volga, Urals and Siberian regions.
They also proposed planting 57 million hectares to grain, up from 53.7 million sown this year, as well as increasing mineral fertiliser use and using high-yield seeds.
Russia's farm sector is struggling to cope with reforms and is ridden with Soviet-era waste and inefficiency.
